<thought>The spectrum shows a strong M peak at 114, an M+1 peak at ~6.7 % of the base, and very small higher peaks. This M+1 intensity corresponds to roughly 6 % per carbon, indicating the presence of several carbon atoms. No 3:1 (Cl) or 1:1 (Br) patterns, nor the ~4 % M+2 of sulfur, are observed. Thus carbon is the only element that can be definitively identified from the isotopic distribution.</thought>
<final_answer>['C']</final_answer>
